etymology: Webster 1828 treats because as a compound of by and cause: by the cause; on this account; for the reason named in the next clause. Cause being a noun, because may be followed by of. His own biblical illustrations are Romans 8:10 (the Spirit is life, because of righteousness) and the wrath that comes because of the children of disobedience. This page fills the KJV-gap conjunction. Companion pages already treat cause, therefore, and wherefore.
biblical_def: Because in Scripture is not a shrug and not a mood. It names the real ground of a real act. John will not let love begin in the lover: We love him, because he first loved us (1 John 4:19). Paul will not let life in the saints be a self-help pulse: the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness (Rom 8:10). Jesus will not let the crowd dress hunger as discipleship: Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled (John 6:26). The Sermon will not let the gate be wide: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it (Matt 7:14). John writes fathers, young men, and little children because ye have known him that is from the beginning (1 John 2:13) — knowledge of the Father, not a feeling, is the ground. The dictionary therefore keeps because from becoming a therapy word. It is the Bible’s way of saying: this, on this account, and no other.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines BECAUSE as a compound of by and cause: on this account; for the cause explained in the next proposition. He notes that because may be followed by of, and illustrates from Romans 8:10 and the wrath that comes because of disobedience.
webster_full: BECAUSE, becauz'. A compound word. [See By and Cause.]

By cause, or by the cause; on this account; for the cause which is explained in the next proposition; for the reason next explained. Thus, I fled, because I was afraid, is to be thus resolved; I fled, by the cause, for the cause, which is mentioned in the next affirmation, viz. I was afraid. Hence, cause being a noun, because may be regularly followed by of.
The spirit is life, because of righteousness.
BECAUSE of these cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience.
scriptures: Matthew 7:14
Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
Romans 8:10
And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.
John 6:26
Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled.
1 John 4:19
We love him, because he first loved us.
1 John 2:13

I write unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I write unto you, young men, because ye have overcome the wicked one. I write unto you, little children, because ye have known the Father.
corruption_summary: Because is corrupted when the ground of love is moved from God’s first love to the self, when loaves are allowed to count as faith, and when the strait gate is treated as optional because the fewness offends modern taste.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to invert 1 John 4:19. Therapeutic religion likes because I feel as the warrant for love, identity, and worship. John will not start there. We love Him because he first loved us. The recovery is monergism in a conjunction: the cause sits in God, not in the lover’s pulse.

The second corruption is the loaves. John 6:26 names a crowd that follows because it ate. Prosperity talk and attractional religion keep the same because and call it hunger for God. Jesus separates miracle from meal. Seeking Him for bread is not faith.

The third corruption is to sand Matthew 7:14. Because strait is the gate is the Lord’s own account of why few find life. The religion that must widen the gate treats the fewness as a scandal to be managed. The adverbial ground remains: the way is narrow because He said it is, not because the church failed to widen it.
roots_summary: Webster: by + cause. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek hoti (G3754) at Matthew 7:14, John 6:26, 1 John 4:19, and 1 John 2:13; Greek dia (G1223) at Romans 8:10 (because of sin / because of righteousness). No Hebrew number is minted on this page. Companion pages treat cause, therefore, and wherefore.
roots_lines: Greek hoti (G3754) — that, because, since (Matt 7:14; John 6:26; 1 John 4:19; 1 John 2:13).
Greek dia (G1223) — through, on account of (Rom 8:10, because of sin / because of righteousness).
Webster’s English compound remains by + cause; this page does not invent a Hebrew lemma for the English conjunction.
Romans 8:10 tags the two because of clauses as G1223; the copula and the nouns sit on other numbers in the same verse line.
usage: We love him, because he first loved us (1 John 4:19) — the cause of Christian love is God’s prior love, not the lover’s mood.
The body is dead because of sin; the Spirit is life because of righteousness (Rom 8:10).
Crowds that come because of loaves are not disciples (John 6:26); the strait gate remains strait because He said so (Matt 7:14).

etymology: Webster 1828 points AMONG / AMONGST to a Greek mixing-word and to mingle: in a general sense, mixed or mingled with, as tares among wheat; then conjoined or associated with, making part of the number (Blessed art thou among women); then of the number, as not one among a thousand. This page fills the KJV-gap preposition. Companion pages already treat people, church, and gentile.
biblical_def: Among in Scripture locates a person inside a people, not above them and not outside them. The Lord’s own rule for greatness is local: it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister (Matt 20:26). Paul will not let the church pretend it is cleaner than the street when it is not: it is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles (1 Cor 5:1). Peter will not let the flock be surprised: there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you (2 Pet 2:1). Jesus locates John inside the old covenant’s highest rank and then outranks him from the kingdom side: Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist (Matt 11:11). The psalm remembers the exodus as extraction: And brought out Israel from among them (Ps 136:11). The dictionary therefore keeps among from becoming a slogan of inclusion without holiness. It is the Bible’s way of saying: in the midst of this people, for their good or for their judgment.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines AMONG / AMONGST as mixed or mingled with (tares among wheat); conjoined or associated with, making part of the number (Blessed art thou among women); and of the number (not one among a thousand).
webster_full: 1. In a general or primitive sense, mixed or mingled with; as tares among wheat.
2. Conjoined or associated with, or making part of the number. Blessed art thou among women.
3. Of the number; as, there is not one among a thousand, possessing the like qualities.
scriptures: Matthew 20:26
But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;
Matthew 11:11
Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
1 Corinthians 5:1
It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife.
2 Peter 2:1

But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction.
Psalm 136:11
And brought out Israel from among them: for his mercy endureth for ever:
corruption_summary: Among is corrupted when greatness among the saints is recast as celebrity, when sin among the church is renamed inclusion, and when false teachers among you are treated as one more voice in a conversation rather than a damnable heresy inside the flock.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to invert Matthew 20:26. The Gentiles lord it; the church is told it shall not be so among you. Platform religion keeps the preposition and loses the ministry. Greatness among the saints is service, not a brand.

The second corruption is to hear 1 Corinthians 5:1 as a diversity report. Paul names fornication among you as a scandal worse than the Gentiles’ catalog. The reading that blesses the sin as identity treats presence in the body as the moral fact. Paul treats holiness in the body as the moral fact and commands the wicked person put away.

The third corruption is to recast 2 Peter 2:1 as a conversation. False teachers are among you, not visiting from another department. Progressive evangelical talk prefers many voices. Peter names damnable heresies and the Lord they deny. The preposition here is a warning, not a welcome mat.
roots_summary: Webster: mixed / mingled with (see Mingle). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek en (G1722) at Matthew 20:26, Matthew 11:11, 1 Corinthians 5:1, and 2 Peter 2:1; Hebrew tavek (H8432) at Psalm 136:11 (from among them). Exodus 29:45 and Leviticus 26:12 leave English among untagged in this cache; no Hebrew number is minted for those two. Companion pages treat people, church, and gentile.
roots_lines: Greek en (G1722) — in, among (Matt 20:26; Matt 11:11; 1 Cor 5:1; 2 Pet 2:1).
Exodus 29:45 and Leviticus 26:12 untagged on the word among in this cache — no Hebrew number is invented.
Psalm 82:1 tags a different English among as H7130 (qereb, inward part) on another verse line; this page does not collapse H8432 and H7130.
usage: Greatness among you is ministry, not lordship (Matt 20:26).
Fornication among you is a church scandal, not a welcome (1 Cor 5:1).
False teachers arise among you (2 Pet 2:1); Israel was brought out from among them by mercy (Ps 136:11).

etymology: Webster 1828 points AWAY to way: absent; at a distance; much used with verbs of going or sending from; as an exclamation, a command to depart (Away with him); and in the older phrase I cannot away with it, I cannot bear it. This page fills the KJV-gap adverb. Companion pages already treat depart, pass, and word. The noun way is a separate head.
biblical_def: Away in Scripture is not a mood of distance. It is removal, departure, or the thing that will not be removed. John the Baptist does not offer a milder Lamb: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world (John 1:29). Jesus will not let creation outlast His speech: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away (Matt 24:35). He will not let the Eleven treat His going as abandonment: It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you (John 16:7). The last city is not therapy; it is subtraction of death: God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes — for the former things are passed away (Rev 21:4). He will not let marriage be dissolved at will: Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery (Matt 19:9). The dictionary therefore keeps away from becoming a slogan of self-care exits. It is the Bible’s way of saying: this is taken off, this departs, this must not be sent off.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines AWAY as absent, at a distance; used with verbs of going or sending from; as an exclamation, a command to depart (Away with him); and in I cannot away with it, I cannot bear or endure it (Isaiah 1).
webster_full: 1. Absent; at a distance; as, the master is away from home. Have me away for I am wounded. 2 Chronicles 35:23.

2. It is much used with words signifying moving or going from; as, go away, send away, run away, etc.; all signifying departure, or separation to a distance. Sometimes without the verb; as, whither away so fast.
3. As an exclamation, it is a command or invitation to depart; away, that is, be gone, or let us go. Away with him. Take him away.
5. Away with has a peculiar signification in the phrase, I cannot away with it. The sense is, I cannot bear or endure it.
scriptures: John 1:29
The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
Matthew 24:35
Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
John 16:7
Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
Revelation 21:4
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
Matthew 19:9
And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.
corruption_summary: Away is corrupted when taking away sin is recast as taking away shame, when heaven and earth passing away is used to relativize Christ’s words, and when putting away a wife is treated as a private exit rather than adultery except for fornication.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to hear John 1:29 as relief from embarrassment. The Lamb taketh away the sin of the world — guilt before God, not a bruise to self-regard. Therapeutic religion prefers a lamb who takes away low self-image. John points at Jesus as sin-bearer.

The second corruption is to invert Matthew 24:35. Modern talk lets Scripture pass away with cultures while the earth is treated as the lasting thing. Jesus says the opposite. Heaven and earth go. His words do not.

The third corruption is to make Matthew 19:9 a lifestyle clause. No-fault exits keep the verb and lose the exception. He names putting away and remarriage as adultery, save for fornication. The recovery is the creational bond, not a softer adverb of departure.

A fourth corruption is to treat John 16:7 as divine absence. The Son goes away in order that the Comforter come. Cessationist recovery still confesses the Spirit sent; it does not turn the going into a hole where private revelation must rush in.

roots_lines: Greek airo (G142) — to lift, take up, take away (John 1:29, taketh away the sin).
Greek parerchomai (G3928) — to pass by, pass away (Matt 24:35).
Greek exaleipho (G1813) — to wipe off, wipe away (Rev 21:4); Greek apoluo (G630) — to loose, send away, put away (Matt 19:9).
Isaiah 53:6 untagged on English away in this cache — no Hebrew number is invented for this page from that verse.
usage: The Lamb taketh away the sin of the world (John 1:29) — sin, not embarrassment.
Heaven and earth shall pass away; His words shall not (Matt 24:35).
He goes away that the Comforter may come (John 16:7); putting away a wife except for fornication is adultery (Matt 19:9).
